prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with wrist fracture after a sideswipe while changing lanes. The patient had 4 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1167; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: Treatment summary. The patient was seen for a wrist injury reported after a sideswipe while changing lanes. Over four office visits, care followed a routine course of immobilization, imaging review, and gradual return to activity, with visit frequency tapering as symptoms eased and function improved. Some examination findings are consistent with a bony injury, including localized tenderness and reduced grip strength, while other tests, including neurovascular checks and motion in adjacent joints, were within normal limits. The patient reports a mild strain in the same region years earlier, which resolved fully without lasting limitation. Billing records for this episode show no repeated or duplicate charges for the same services. Given the low-speed nature of the contact described, the severity of the reported injury appears out of step with the mechanism, and this should be weighed alongside the objective findings.
